title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page closes section 3, on the moduli of curves of a fixed 'combinatorial type' G, and opens section 4, on Mumford–Deligne stable curves.

(1) Remark (NB), with the margin note '(g, ν = card J) admissible', meaning 2g−2+ν>0. M_{g,J} is the moduli multiplicity (stack) of smooth genus-g curves with points marked by the finite set J. Choosing a bijection {1,…,ν} ≅ J identifies M_{g,J} with M^!_{g,ν}. The '!' presumably means numbered (ordered) markings. The identification is compatible with the actions of S_J and S_ν.

(2) Since M^!_{g,ν} is smooth of finite type over Spec Z (Deligne–Mumford), so is each M_{g,J}.

(3) The previous page gives (23), an equivalence M_G ≃ ∏_α M_{g_α, I_α} over the vertices α of a semi-stable dual graph G. Here I_α is the set of half-edges plus marked points at α. Hence M_G is smooth of finite type over Z. So is the 'mixed multiplicity' M_[G] = (M_G, Γ), with Γ = Aut G acting; in modern terms this is the quotient stack [M_G/Aut G].

In modern language, M_[G] is the locally closed boundary stratum of \bar M_{g,ν} with dual graph G, up to normalization. Its smoothness follows from the product decomposition.

(4) Section 4 defines a relative 'MD-curve' (X, I) over a schematic multiplicity S:
- X → S is proper, flat and of finite presentation.
- I ⊂ X is a closed subscheme, flat and of finite presentation over S.
- Geometric fibres are connected 1-dimensional curves whose only singularities are ordinary double points not lying in I.
- A rigidity (stability) condition holds: no smooth genus-1 fibre with I empty, and every genus-0 component carries marked weight (marked points plus branches) ≥ 3.

This is Knudsen's notion of a stable ν-pointed curve, with the marking given as an unordered subscheme rather than as sections. The next page notes that the dual graph type can now vary from fibre to fibre, while (g, ν) is locally constant by invariance of χ(O) and of card I_s.

The purpose is to set up \bar M_{g,ν} and its stratification at infinity by the stacks M_[G], for the study of the 'structure à l'infini' (the Teichmüller tower programme of the Esquisse).
errors: Minor gap: I must be required to have fibres that are finite, reduced and contained in the smooth locus. Otherwise 'card I_s' and 'marked points' are not meaningful (equivalently, I should be finite étale over S). Flat of finite presentation plus the stated fibre conditions nearly gives this, but reducedness of I_s is not stated explicitly on this page.
Smoothness of M_{g,J} holds only for admissible (g, ν), i.e. 2g−2+ν>0. The marginal note '(g,ν=card J) admissible' supplies this hypothesis.
Smoothness 'of finite type over Z' must be understood for stacks (multiplicities), not coarse schemes. This is consistent with Grothendieck's usage.

ideas.what: Smoothness and finite type over Z of the moduli stacks of smooth pointed curves, with set-indexed markings M_{g,J} ≅ M_{g,ν}
ideas.modern_name: M_{g,n} as a smooth Deligne–Mumford stack over Z

ideas.what: Strata M_G ≅ ∏ M_{g_α,I_α} and M_[G] = [M_G/Aut G], hence smooth
ideas.modern_name: Boundary strata of \bar M_{g,n} indexed by stable graphs; gluing maps ξ_G
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) alludes to the stratification at infinity of M_{g,ν}, without these details

ideas.what: Definition of relative MD-curve (X, I) over a base multiplicity, with I a closed subscheme (unordered marking) and the stability condition
ideas.modern_name: Stable marked curves (Knudsen stable n-pointed curves, with unordered markings)

deep.surprise_reason: Standard foundational material on M_{g,ν}, its boundary strata indexed by dual graphs, and stable pointed curves. It is well established in the literature (Deligne–Mumford, Knudsen, ACG). The only Grothendieck-specific flavour is the stack language of 'multiplicités' and unordered markings via a subscheme I.
